paragraphs: He is mentioned in Yalkut, Esther, 1056, speaking in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, who heard from his teacher [that Ahasuerus’s scepter stretched two hundred cubits]. Hyman calls this a scribal error and proposes Rabbah bar Rav Ofran, as in Megillah 15b, and so it is in Midrash Lekach Tov.

notes.text: ר״א בן שמוע is rendered Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua. The square brackets are in the source.

Megillah 15b in the consulted edition gives Rabbah bar Ofran and Rabbi Elazar without a patronymic. It includes another link in the chain of transmission before the figure of two hundred. Hyman reports the Yalkut and Lekach Tov readings.
